newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Drivers stick it out in snowbound Caucasus tunnel.
newsitem.headline: Drivers stick it out in snowbound Caucasus tunnel.

text.p: Emergency workers on Saturday cleared the road north from a tunnel in the Caucasus mountains into Russia but some 30 truckers, headed south into Georgia, are staying with their vehicles after over a week trapped by snow.

A spokesman for the Emergencies Ministry in Moscow said the drivers were refusing to abandon their loads in the Roksky Tunnel, 3,000 metres (10,000 feet) up in the hills, even though they could now drive back to the Russian town of Vladikavkaz.
Snow clearance on the southbound side of the pass, in the separatist Georgian province of South Ossetia, had not been completed, preventing them from driving on south into Georgia.
Rescue workers have battled gales, fog and snow since last Friday to clear avalanches and snowdrifts up to 12 metres (40 feet) deep that trapped over 200 travellers in the tunnel.
The vast majority were freed on New Year's Day and airlifted to Vladikavkaz on Friday once the weather cleared slightly.
Two women were reported to have given birth in the tunnel, and one of the babies was said to have died.
The truckers have received food, clothing and medical supplies.
Patrols fired anti-aircraft cannon on Saturday to dislodge dangerous overhangs of snow that could cause new avalanches.
